summary: A 14-by-14-foot ground cabin on Bateman Butte in Douglas County, Oregon, staffed in the 1930s and 1960s and gone after 1965; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 14-by-14-foot cab set on rocks at ground level, not a tower
facts.status_note: Lookout house dismantled in 1965 per Forest Lookouts; Firelookout says destroyed. No source describes the site today.

events.note: Oregon Department of Forestry annual report recommends a lookout house at Bateman Butte
Register gives 1933 as the build year for the 14-by-14-foot cab
August 1934 forest supervisor's memo to the regional forester: ground house set on rocks, job done; Firelookout dates the L-4 cab to 1934
Forrest Emmitt stationed at the lookout for the season
Army AWS station at the lookout active May 10 to October 16, 1943, tied to the Roseburg Filter Center
Peggy Meacham transferred from Mt. Scott lookout to Bateman
Leta Petheram takes the summer post at Bateman
Not staffed in 1965; discontinued after fire season; house dismantled. Register says removed; Firelookout says destroyed
Registered November 18, 2010, nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says the cab was built in 1933; Firelookout dates the L-4 cab to 1934 and Forest Lookouts logs the house as finished in 1934. The story gives both and lists 1934 as the build event.
Firelookout says 21 miles northwest; the 1953 survey note on Forest Lookouts says about 22 miles. Both are kept in the story.
Forest Lookouts says the house was dismantled; Firelookout says destroyed; the register says removed. The story keeps all three.

notes_for_editor: Brief shows only the 2010 registration; the build and removal events are added from Forest Lookouts and Firelookout. Build year (1933 vs 1934) and fate wording conflict across sources. The brief's access 'unknown' is kept; no source describes the site now. Brief distance and elevation match the register. The August 1934 document is a memo from the Umpqua forest supervisor to the regional forester, not a work report.
